units.translation: We marvel at your tongue, how bold-mouthed it is.
But you have a tongue opposite to Orpheus.
But to pluck for me this vain tongue in this way.
In place of a hostile tongue, let a hostile tongue be accomplished.
I advise you to keep a tongue of good omen.
Do not cast upon the ground the fruit of a vain tongue.
A soothing charm and enchantment of my tongue.
Because he watches over my tongue and mouth.
You find the path of a good tongue.
You hear clear words from a free-speaking tongue.
Everyone among the resident aliens bears a ready tongue for evil.
For the gods do not hear justice from the tongue.
Be silent, lest someone learn of it, and for the sake of the tongue report all these things.
And indeed from us the roar of the Persian tongue met them.
Imitating the cry of the Phocian tongue.
ox
the tongue, outrunning the heart, would pour out everything
no longer
tongue
a goad of the tongue
a goad of madness
not being able to keep silent
nor to lie for the sake of the tongue
through excessive and useless impulse of the tongue
to send forth a Dorian tongue
spearhead
spearhead
the double tongue of the shaft.
jaw
jaw
Figuratively of the force of fire
of skin diseases consuming the body
Of the edge of iron
Of the jaws of the Propontis
They snatched many false banquets from the raging jaw.
Lichens, devouring the ancient nature, mounting upon the flesh with wild jaws.
Rivers of fire devouring with wild jaws.
The fierce jaw of fire.
The stubborn jaw of the adamantine wedge.
The rough Salmydessian jaw of the sea.
to bend
to bend, i.e. κάμπτω
A frequent verb among the epic poets, on which see Thes. vol. 2 p. 669.
For he will bend nothing of these things for me, so as even to speak.
to bend
to card
to card
about which passage I spoke in Philologus vol. 13 p. 489. Attic usage requires κναπτόμενοι, about which I spoke in Thes. s.v.
carded by the terrible sea.
carded
fuller
fuller
where I restored the Attic form κναφεύς, about which it is said in Thes.
The fuller and the feeder had the same end.
fuller
opinion
opinion
Thus Eurip. Herc. fur. 408: ἓν δὲ πάντων γνῶμα ταυτὸν ἐμπρέπει [one opinion of all is conspicuous].
Being a partner of such an opinion.
one opinion of all is conspicuous
opinion
opinion, judgment
mind, spirit, intelligence
will, counsel
Fear was upon all the barbarians, deprived of their judgment.
K. And indeed tell me this, not against my judgment. A. Know that I will not corrupt my judgment.
I tell you my opinion.
You have set upright the judgment of your mouth.
To err from a prudent judgment.
I now bid these men to cast a just vote according to their judgment.
May it turn out well, against my judgment.
Without judgment they did everything.
He will be blunted in judgment.
He was wise, who first bore this in his mind.
When judgment is absent, great calamity occurs.
Fortune is common, but judgment belongs to those who possess it.
Guiding this omen by judgment without bridles.
